page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps under a KVM hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.e4.xlarge sits in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance scored 950.58, which is in the bottom 10%, while multi-core performance reached 3679.45, placing it in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show 30.12 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 22.11 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Database and key-value operations, such as Redis SET, achieved 5.32 million operations per second, which is categorized in the bottom 25% of tested instances.

Given its shared CPU allocation and older Intel Xeon architecture, this instance exhibits lower compute density and processing speeds, as evidenced by its poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and weak LLM inference metrics. However, its high memory capacity relative to vCPUs makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained high-performance CPU throughput. Appropriate workloads include caching layers, lightweight database hosting, static web serving, and general-purpose memory-heavy applications.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.xlarge is an x86_64 server instance utilizing an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 shared vCPUs (2 physical cores) and 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data places this instance in the lower performance tiers, with stress-ng single-core performance in the bottom 10% and multi-core performance in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also modest, with large-block reads at 30.12 GB/sec. Due to its shared CPU architecture and weak computational benchmarks, the ecs.e4.xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive but compute-light workloads, such as caching layers, small database operations, and static web serving where high memory capacity is required without demanding sustained CPU performance.
